clues.text: In Babylon, a chief official gave this young man from Judah a new name in place of Hananiah.
At Daniel's request, King Nebuchadnezzar appointed him to help manage the province of Babylon.
He was one of the Jews accused of refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue in Babylon.
He told Nebuchadnezzar that even if God did not rescue him, he would not worship the golden statue.
Nebuchadnezzar's face changed toward him in rage, and the king ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter.
Nebuchadnezzar saw a fourth figure, like a son of the gods, walking with him unharmed in the fire.
When he came out of Nebuchadnezzar's furnace, not a hair of his head was singed and he had no smell of fire.
